text:
Dougie Hamilton is 33, in his fifth season in New Jersey, and playing a quieter role than the power-play weapon he used to be. He has one power-play point this season, 10 points overall in 21 games, and about 20 and a half minutes a night. His overtime-forcing goal against the Islanders on Nov. 7 was a reminder the shot is still there; his top shot of nearly 95 mph ranks in the 88th percentile by NHL EDGE.

The numbers say he's fine, not declining. The Devils get 57% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, right in line with the team, and his scoring rate sits in the middle of our talent range. He's shooting 3.7%, a little below his norm, and his line has scored 3.8 fewer goals than its chances. A few more pucks should go in.

Defense is where he's underrated. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 18% of entries aimed at him last season, against 11% for a typical defenseman, and Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 97th percentile. On a team that has won eight of ten, he's a steady piece rather than the headline.
